intro: Sunset Park is a Lakeway subdivision of 2000s mid sized homes. West facing glass here shows every streak at the end of the day, and our pure water finish is built to handle it.

sections.h2: What Sunset Park homes are like
paragraphs: The homes are mid sized, between 2,187 and 2,900 square feet, built in the 2000s and priced from $500K to $650K. The neighborhood has no known gate or HOA. For a typical Lakeway buyer, this sits in the middle of the market, with enough space for a family.
After two decades, landscaping is full, fences are weathered and many owners have updated kitchens or paint. Windows are often the one item that has gone uncleaned for years.

sections.h2: What Sunset Park windows deal with
paragraphs: West facing glass takes strong afternoon light in a neighborhood like this one. Any smear stands out when the sun drops low. Pollen settles heavily on those panes, cedar from December to February and live oak from March to April.

Twenty years of sprinklers leave a visible mineral layer on lower windows. On 2000s homes we often see old hard water stains that regular washing will not lift. Spot removal costs $10 per pane. Tracks collect webs and leaf bits, and screens loosen with age.

We arrive with the pole system and work from the ground, reaching up to three stories. No ladders touch the siding or stucco for exterior glass. Interior windows are done by hand with squeegees. Gutters on mid sized 2000s homes are often packed with seeds by now, so owners often add them. We fit this neighborhood in with other north and central Lakeway work.

A 2,500 square foot home in Sunset Park is about $250 for the exterior. Plan on about two hours outside and 75 minutes inside. Pairing interior with exterior comes to $15 per window. Triannual takes 15% off and lines up with the cedar and live oak seasons.
